item.title: Is an expired medicine sitting on your pharmacy shelf right now?
item.description:
Is an expired medicine sitting on your pharmacy shelf right now?
A survey of 100 pharmacists in Delhi, published in the Indian Journal of Pharmacology in 2016, found only 53% agreed there was a system to remove expired medicines from stock. Without one, expiry is checked by eye and found too late.
A simple weekly expiry check for a hospital pharmacy: • List every batch expiring in the next 90 days. • Flag expired stock that is still on the shelf and remove it the same day. • Issue the batch that expires first, first. • Record the batch number and expiry date the moment new stock arrives. • Check items at or below reorder level, so you buy only what you will use.

item.title: India's factory PMI just hit 56.0, a nine month high.
item.description:
India's factory PMI just hit 56.0, a nine month high.
The HSBC Flash India Manufacturing PMI rose to 56.0 in November 2026, up from 54.7 in October. Any reading above 50 means growth. New orders grew at the fastest pace since June, and factories added staff at the fastest rate in seven months.
Why it matters for an owner: • More orders means more raw material to buy on time. • More work orders to plan without missing dispatch dates. • More invoices to raise and follow up before dues pile up.
What to do: make it a weekly check, not a month end scramble. Look at items below reorder level, open orders, and who owes you money. If finding those three numbers takes more than a few minutes, the records are too spread out.

item.title: Fee day should not mean a queue at the school office.
item.description:
Fee day should not mean a queue at the school office.
India's private unaided schools now teach 9.89 crore students, up from 9 crore two years earlier (Ministry of Education UDISE+ 2025-26 report, as reported by PTI). More students means more fees to raise, collect and follow up.
A simple fee day checklist for school offices: • Raise the month's fees for every class before fee day, not on the counter. • Give a numbered receipt for every payment, whatever the mode: UPI, cash, cheque or bank. • Settle the oldest dues first, so the dues list stays honest. • Check one defaulters list every week instead of calling every parent. • Send a polite reminder the same day a fee goes overdue.

item.title: MSMEs make 48.58% of India's exports.
item.description:
MSMEs make 48.58% of India's exports.
That is nearly half of everything India sells abroad, according to a PIB document published in June 2026 (January 2026 data). The same document says registrations on the Udyam portal and Udyam Assist platform have crossed 8.7 crore.
Why it matters for an owner: • Export buyers expect clean GST invoices and on time delivery. • Stock numbers have to match what is really on the shelf. • Dues have to be followed up before they hurt cash flow.
What to do: pick one weekly check. Pending invoices, stock below reorder level, and who owes you money. If it takes more than a few minutes, the records are too spread out.

item.title: ₹4 lakh vanished from a factory. Can you guess where?
item.description:
₹4 lakh vanished from a factory. Can you guess where?
An illustrative example many manufacturers will recognise: • The supplier was short by 20 kg. Not it. • The machines lost their usual 1.5%. Not it. • The store room matched the register. Not it. • The night shift was losing 7.5%, against about 1.5% on the other shifts.
Nobody saw it because yield was checked once a year. A daily yield report for each shift would have shown it in the first week.
